assertions: Canonical procedural acts and procedural questions produce source-time-ordered events.
Every procedural event retains its source act, utterance, source intervals, evidence spans, observed attribution, target state, effects, confidence, and review.
Every procedural event produces exactly one immutable contiguous snapshot.
Observed acoustic speaker remains distinct from procedurally recognized speaker.
Pronouns do not automatically identify floor recipients.
A floor grant can open an active response interval while its target remains unresolved.
Explicit turn yield and time-expiration events close the active response interval.
Answer requests preserve bounded pending-question targets.
Warnings and expiration remain distinct timing events.
Moderator instructions, clarification requests, topic transitions, technical interruptions, and unresolved events remain explicit state.
Every state change is linked to a discourse act and source-media interval.
Violation, fault, blame, and sanction fields are constrained to false or zero.
Procedural-state run and report artifacts are sealed, replayable, and reusable.
CLI operations build, validate, inspect, and list events, snapshots, and unresolved procedural events.
Schema export includes all five procedural-state contracts.
limitations: Recognized speaker remains unresolved without explicit procedural target evidence.
Pending questions persist until an explicit later procedural event changes state.
Granted extensions require explicit structured evidence and are not inferred from generic wording.
The controlled fixtures qualify state mechanics, not natural-conversation procedural accuracy.
